slides.texte_overlay:
Everyday habits that earn
you instant respect
Holding the door and making eye contact. Small courtesy, done naturally, every time. People notice manners long before they notice anything else.
Admitting when you don't know. "Good question, I'll find out." Honest uncertainty earns more respect than a confident guess that turns out wrong.
Keeping your cool in traffic, queues and delays. Calm in small frustrations shows people exactly how you'll behave when real pressure arrives.
Remembering what people told you last time. "How did your sister's wedding go?" Paying attention is a form of respect people return immediately.
Always learning something. I do five minutes a day of history, art or science, and people respect a man who keeps his mind sharp and curious.
slides.texte_sophia: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. People respect a man who keeps his mind sharp and curious.

slides.texte_overlay: Dressing clean on ordinary days. Not fancy, just tidy. Looking put together on a normal Tuesday shows you respect yourself and the people around you.
Never talking down to anyone. The cashier, the intern, the security guard. Treating everyone as equals is the fastest way to be respected by all.
